chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Asbahani, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him while I was listening: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I find weakness in my body.' He said to him: 'Stick to milk, for it builds flesh and strengthens bone.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam recommend for physical weakness and body strengthening?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, a companion reports physical weakness to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who prescribes milk as a therapeutic remedy for its ability to build flesh and strengthen bones. This narration highlights the Prophetic tradition of utilizing natural dietary elements for physical healing, a concept deeply rooted in Shia medical jurisprudence. The emphasis on milk underscores its status as a complete, nourishing food source endorsed by the Imams for maintaining bodily strength.
